audit.whatIsWrong: The chart handed Sion Levels 3, 4-5 and the first item while every prose line on the page describes Renekton winning those stages ('decided in your favor every time', 'turning his biggest threat into a missed opportunity', 'keep trading short and banking the health gap'). The packet chart also gives Renekton Levels 1 through 5.
audit.why: Sion is immobile with a telegraphed charge; Renekton's E lets him leave every trade. Nothing at Level 3 or 4-5 favours Sion, and the 51.58% win rate over 2187 games backs the early Renekton lane.
audit.corrected: Levels 2, 3 and 4-5 flipped to Renekton (7/10) and First item to Skill (5/10), in both layers as one atomic group. Level 6 kept as Renekton against the packet's 'Skill' because Dominus versus an immobile target is the page's stated kill window and both layers already agreed.

audit.why: Level 2, level 6 Dominus, first-item bruiser spike, and Sion's late HP wall — four spikes present and correctly ordered against his scaling.
audit.corrected: No structural change; spike text left intact where accurate.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells the player to 'open with a quick non-empowered auto or Q to pop' Soul Furnace, and claims the shield 'pops on the first hit'. Neither is true: Soul Furnace is a durable shield, and Renekton's empowered W (above 50 Fury) destroys damage shields on the target outright.
audit.why: The current advice wastes the opening of every trade and leaves the shield up. The real sequence is the opposite — bank 50 Fury first, then the W deletes the shield and stuns for 1.5s.
audit.corrected: Shield destruction stated in whys[3], phases[2].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[1].d, report[5].t, mid and wants.foe[1].

edits.before: Levels 4-6 is where you need to cash the lead. His Soul Furnace (W) shield absorbs the first hit of a trade, so open with a quick non-empowered auto or Q to pop it before you spend your empowered W-stun — otherwise half your burst is wasted. Keep the wave pushed slightly past mid-lane so he has to walk up and channel Q in the open where you can read it. At level 6 Dominus is nearly a free kill: his immobility means he cannot avoid your extended all-in, and the rapid Fury generation lets you chain two empowered Ws back-to-back; respect his passive zombie state after the kill — disengage the moment he drops to let it expire safely.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 is where you need to cash the lead. Soul Furnace (W) absorbs your burst only if you arrive at low fury: empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields, so 50 Fury deletes it outright and stuns 1.5s — never open with a chip auto to 'pop' it. Keep the wave pushed slightly past mid-lane so he has to walk up and charge Q in the open where you can read it. At level 6 Dominus is nearly a free kill: his immobility means he cannot avoid your all-in, and the Fury ramp chains two empowered Ws; respect his zombie passive after the kill — disengage the moment he drops and let it expire.

edits.before: Stack his passive HP and pop Soul Furnace shield in every trade to absorb your Q-heal burst
edits.after: Catch you below 50 Fury so Soul Furnace survives — an unempowered W cannot break the shield

notes: Two things worth the user's attention. First, the shield advice on this page was actively harmful: it told the player to spend the opening of every trade chipping a shield that empowered W deletes for free. Second, the chart disagreed with its own prose on three rows; I flipped them to Renekton per the packet chart, but deliberately kept Level 6 as Renekton where the packet says Skill, because both layers already agreed and the Dominus window is the page's stated win condition — flag if you want the packet followed literally there instead.
